text:
sarah: Heads up, Acme POC asked for a clear incident response (IR) and breach-notify runbook we can include in the SOW. They specifically want: notification timelines, who gets CC'd, what we will/ won't do for on-prem vs hosted, and cost expectations for forensics. Can we put together a short Slack-ready summary for sales to include?

mike: Yup. High-level bullets below — I’ll keep it POC-friendly.

mike: - Hosted API: acknowledge within 72h of detection; initial triage within 72h; estimated full incident report within 7-30 days depending on scope. For POC we target 7-14 days for the initial report.

mike: - Private / On-prem / VPC: we notify customer within 72h of confirming an issue in our software; customer owns infrastructure-level forensics unless SOW includes forensic services. We can provide guidance and artifact extraction steps.

julia: - Dedicated (reserved capacity): prioritized triage (24-48h initial), can include deeper telemetry exports if subscribed in SOW.

lee: - Legal guidance: we will not commit to regulator filings (e.g., GDPR 72h) unless contractually obligated. "Notify" timelines are fine but avoid promising regulator submissions.

nina: - CC list for initial POC notification: Customer security lead, customer legal (if provided), CS rep, AE, and internal escalation: lee (legal), nina (CS), security on-call, and ir-bot to open an incident ticket.

omar: question: if customer asks for SIG/CAIQ answers during an IR, what's our stance?

mike: We can provide our completed SIG/CAIQ and supporting artifacts (SOC/pen test summaries, config exports, relevant logs) as attachments. For running ad-hoc evidence collection during an incident (e.g., live forensic imaging), that's billable unless in SOW.

lee: Also note: redact any customer data when sharing artifacts. Use access control links for artifact storage.

sarah: finance/policy Q: will we ever pay for a customer's third-party forensics?

lee: Not as a baseline for POCs. Exception paths exist: discount or limited credit for strategic deals, must be pre-approved by revenue ops and legal.

nina: mitigation checklist for customers to include in initial notify:
- rotate keys/credentials
- disable affected endpoints
- collect session IDs and correlate with our timeline
- preserve logs (do not purge)

mike: recommend including this short notify template in SOWs and POC docs.

sarah: can someone paste a one-paragraph blurb we can drop in the SOW?

mike: Drop-in SOW blurb: "Redwood Inference Incident Response: Redwood will notify the designated customer security contact within 72 hours of confirming a security incident affecting customer data or service availability. For Hosted customers, Redwood provides initial triage and periodic updates; a full incident report will typically be delivered within 7-30 days, with POCs targeted at 7-14 days. For Private/VPC or on-prem deployments, Redwood will notify the customer and provide remote assistance for artifact collection; on-prem forensic work is the customer's responsibility unless otherwise stated in the SOW. For Dedicated Reserved Capacity customers, Redwood provides prioritized incident triage and expanded telemetry support. Any forensic services performed by Redwood beyond initial triage are billable unless explicitly included in the SOW. Redwood will coordinate with customer security and legal contacts and follow agreed escalation paths."

julia: nice and concise. sales can use this as a default clause.

sarah: thanks team. @omar can you attach the SIG/CAIQ PDF when you send this to Acme?

omar: will do. also creating ticket now.
